name: @nestxapp/ato-mcp

tools.name: ato_whoami
tools.description: Returns the caller identity (AssigneeId/Role/AiModel) resolved from the configured API key. Before working on any task, read your role working guide (ato_playbook; also sent as this server's instructions) and follow it.

tools.name: ato_playbook
tools.description: Returns the working guide of your role (how to do your job with rigor: evidence, severities, when to escalate), as set by your company or the ATO default. Read it before your first task and whenever you are unsure.

tools.name: ato_resume
tools.description: Resumes this assignee open work: in_progress/changes_requested/qa_rejected tasks + last 10 events.

tools.name: ato_task_context
tools.description: Full detail for a task: acceptance criteria, ContextSnapshot, timeline, evidence, comments, and the project flow: task.workflow (useCodeReview, useQa, useReadyToDeploy, ordered stages) and task.nextStatusOnSubmit (where your submit will send the work).

taskId.description: Task key, typed (e.g. AF-HU-12) or legacy (e.g. AF-80), or GUID.

tools.name: ato_comment
tools.description: Post a comment/suggestion/question/objection/reply on a task (never changes status).

taskId.description: Task key, typed (e.g. AF-HU-12) or legacy (e.g. AF-80), or GUID.

tools.name: ato_debate
tools.description: List the comment/debate thread for a task.

taskId.description: Task key, typed (e.g. AF-HU-12) or legacy (e.g. AF-80), or GUID.

tools.name: ato_attachments
tools.description: List the files attached to a task (name, type, size, purpose, who uploaded it, fileId). Use ato_fetch_attachment to read one.

taskId.description: Task key, typed (e.g. AF-HU-12) or legacy (e.g. AF-80), or GUID.

tools.name: ato_fetch_attachment
tools.description: Download an attached file by fileId into a local folder (default: a temp folder) and return its path, so you can open a mockup or read an evidence file.

instructions: You are an AI teammate in ATO. Your role working guide could not be loaded now; call ato_playbook to read it before you start. Until then: read the whole task and its acceptance criteria before acting; back every claim with verifiable evidence (HTTP response, database query, log, screenshot); only blockers (security, wrong data, unmet criterion, something broken) send a task back, should/nit go as comments; record out-of-scope findings as new tasks; after 2 rounds of changes without closing, escalate to a human with a comment.
